recommendation: Keep the commit as-is. It fixes the active current-build source for the applied issue while preserving later FHIR-36012 code/comment cleanup. If Vocab wants a broader terminology refresh against a newer UCUM/NLM data source, that should be handled as a separate review rather than folded into this capitalization reconciliation.
issue_request: FHIR-33030 was a Published/Persuasive Vocab technical correction for FHIR-core ValueSet/ucum-common, asking that display values for common UCUM codes use consistent capitalization. Jira resolved that UCUM displays should be lower case, with later comments/minutes clarifying that the common value set should line up with the UCUM/NLM example displays rather than arbitrary mixed case.
initial_application: Git commit 931fe86d01 (Applied FHIR-33030) previously normalized many displays in source/valueset/valueset-ucum-common.xml, including the ticket examples. Current source had drifted after later same-file UCUM cleanup and still contained mixed-case displays such as Thousands Per MicroLiter, KiloInternationalUnitsPerMilliLiter, and MICROCURIE.
additional_context: FHIR-36012 later removed UCUM comments and deduplicated stripped common codes in the same value set; that explained how the file changed again but did not supersede FHIR-33030. Build-scope checks showed valueset=ValueSet is active in source/fhir.ini and ValueSet/ucum-common is referenced by the value set examples list. Confluence minutes confirmed the Vocab decision trail, and a 2026 Zulip discussion independently noted current ucum-common inconsistencies without a conflicting work-group decision.
reconciliation: Updated source/valueset/valueset-ucum-common.xml display values back to the FHIR-33030-applied choices for codes still present after FHIR-36012, plus lowercased the stripped-code mU/mmol display that had the same capitalization drift. Historical generated release files were intentionally left untouched.
source_changes: source/valueset/valueset-ucum-common.xml: normalized 130 display values in the active Common UCUM Units value set, including the Jira examples 10*3/uL and g/m2 and later-visible inconsistencies such as k[iU]/mL and uCi.
